title: Equality-Based PIL — Article 14, Arbitrariness and Discrimination (Art. 14)

content.overview: Article 14 equality and non-arbitrariness form a major substantive base for PIL challenging discriminatory or arbitrary State action affecting a class. Liberal standing allows representative claims; the rights base remains equality before the law and equal protection, enforced under Articles 32 and 226.
content.glance: Ask: (1) Classification or arbitrary State action? (2) Class affected? (3) Article 14 engaged? (4) Standing bona fides? (5) Forum 32 or 226?
content.study:
Core rule: Article 14 bars discrimination and supports challenges to arbitrary State action. In PIL, a bona fide petitioner may challenge measures that unequally burden a class unable to litigate individually.

Tests in outline: intelligible differentia and rational relation for classifications; non-arbitrariness for State action. Plead the class, the measure, and the equality defect.

Limits: Not every policy disagreement is Article 14 PIL. Private commercial rivalry and vague equality rhetoric fail abuse screens.

Current-law framing: Articles 14, 32, 226. Case-law verification remains separate.

sections.heading: Article 14 as PIL rights base
sections.body: Equality before the law and equal protection support class-wide challenges to discriminatory or arbitrary public action.

sections.heading: Classification and arbitrariness
sections.body: Challenge formal unequal treatment or arbitrary exercise of power affecting a public class.

sections.heading: Representative standing
sections.body: Bona fide petitioners may enforce Article 14 for classes facing access barriers.

sections.heading: Forum
sections.body: Article 32 for Supreme Court Part III claims; Article 226 for High Court including broader public-law framing.

sections.heading: Abuse filters
sections.body: Equality label does not validate private or motivated petitions.

examples.title: Discriminatory benefit scheme
examples.body: A statutory benefit excludes an identifiable class without rational basis. Representative PIL under Article 14 may seek striking or extension as the law allows.

examples.title: Tender rival as equality PIL
examples.body: Lost bidder frames commercial loss as Article 14 PIL. Private-dispute filter applies.

hypotheticals.question: Is every unfair policy Article 14 PIL?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. There must be a justiciable equality or arbitrariness defect, class injury, and bona fides.

misconceptions.trap: Any inequality of outcome proves Article 14 violation in PIL.
misconceptions.correction: Legal classification and arbitrariness tests still govern.

cases.name: S.P. Gupta v. Union of India
cases.ratioDecidendi: Standing may be relaxed for bona fide public redress.
cases.relevance: Standing for equality PILs; verification open.

cases.name: State of Uttaranchal v. Balwant Singh Chaufal
cases.ratioDecidendi: Credentials, motive, public injury, no personal gain.

cases.name: Bandhua Mukti Morcha v. Union of India
cases.ratioDecidendi: Flexible procedure for effective rights enforcement.
